name: AWS Secrets Manager
description: Protects against destructive AWS Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store \ operations like delete-secret and delete-parameter.

destructive_patterns.name: aws-secretsmanager-delete-secret
destructive_patterns.description: aws secretsmanager delete-secret removes secrets and may cause data loss.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a secret schedules it for deletion (default 30 days) or immediately \ removes it with --force-delete-without-recovery. Applications using this secret \ will fail to authenticate or decrypt data.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws secretsmanager get-secret-value: Export value first \ - aws secretsmanager describe-secret: Check rotation/replication \ - Use --recovery-window-in-days for recoverable deletion

destructive_patterns.name: aws-secretsmanager-delete-resource-policy
destructive_patterns.description: aws secretsmanager delete-resource-policy removes access controls.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a resource policy removes cross-account access and custom permissions. \ Other AWS accounts or services that rely on this policy will lose access to the \ secret immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws secretsmanager get-resource-policy: Export policy first \ - Verify no cross-account dependencies exist \ - Update IAM policies to compensate if needed

destructive_patterns.name: aws-secretsmanager-remove-regions
destructive_patterns.description: aws secretsmanager remove-regions-from-replication can reduce availability.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing regions from replication deletes the secret replica in those regions. \ Applications in removed regions will lose local access to the secret, increasing \ latency or causing failures during cross-region failover.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws secretsmanager describe-secret: Review replica regions \ - Verify no applications in target regions use the secret \ - Update disaster recovery documentation

destructive_patterns.name: aws-secretsmanager-update-secret
destructive_patterns.description: aws secretsmanager update-secret overwrites secret metadata or value.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Updating a secret can change its value, KMS key, or description. The previous \ value becomes a non-current version. Applications using the old value may fail \ if automatic rotation is not configured.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws secretsmanager get-secret-value: Export current value \ - Use put-secret-value to create new version instead \ - Test new value in non-production environment first

destructive_patterns.name: aws-secretsmanager-put-secret-value
destructive_patterns.description: aws secretsmanager put-secret-value creates a new secret version and can break clients.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Creating a new secret version makes it the current value immediately. Applications \ caching the old value will use outdated credentials until they refresh. Rotation \ windows should be coordinated with application deployments.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws secretsmanager get-secret-value: Export current value \ - Use version staging labels for gradual rollout \ - Coordinate secret updates with application deployments

destructive_patterns.name: aws-ssm-delete-parameter
destructive_patterns.description: aws ssm delete-parameter removes a parameter and can break deployments.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an SSM parameter immediately removes it. Applications, CloudFormation \ stacks, and deployment scripts referencing this parameter will fail. There is no \ recovery window like Secrets Manager.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws ssm get-parameter: Export value first \ - aws ssm describe-parameters: Check parameter history \ - Search CloudFormation templates for references

destructive_patterns.name: aws-ssm-delete-parameters
destructive_patterns.description: aws ssm delete-parameters removes parameters and can break deployments.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting multiple SSM parameters at once can break numerous applications and \ deployment pipelines simultaneously. Each parameter is deleted immediately with \ no recovery option.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws ssm get-parameters: Export all values first \ - Delete one parameter at a time to limit blast radius \ - Verify no active deployments use these parameters
